data.about: A glass roof on two columns of different heights, six loads along it, and the truss between them is yours to invent. Whatever you draw, the two reactions are already decided — the loads are all vertical and one bearing is a roller, so the only question global equilibrium can answer is how the 100 kN splits, and it splits 37.5 to 62.5. This view offers one determinate answer, a parallel-chord truss following the fall of the roof, and then solves it joint by joint. Drag its depth and watch every member respond.
